notes.meaning: A wise child listens to a parent's teaching and grows from it. A mocker, on the other hand, refuses even the strongest correction because of stubborn pride. Welcoming correction is the first step toward true wisdom.

Good words bring good rewards back to the speaker, satisfying the heart like wholesome food. Those who are treacherous crave violence and will see that harm bounce back upon their own heads. What we say has real power to bless or hurt us.
Watching what we say protects our whole life from needless trouble. Careless and uncontrolled speech only invites sudden ruin and regret. Thinking before speaking saves a person from guilt and grief.

A lazy person dreams of having much, but ends up with nothing because he will not work. In contrast, those who work hard see their desires fully met and enjoy plenty. This is true for daily work as well as for our spiritual life.

Those who walk uprightly hate lies because deceit goes against God's truth. Wicked people, however, act shamefully and bring disgrace upon themselves and others. An honest life builds trust and protects our good name.
Living with integrity acts like a shield that protects a person from moral ruin. Wickedness, however, drags down the sinner and brings sudden collapse. Doing what is right keeps our steps safe.

Some people pretend to be wealthy when they are actually penniless, while others live modestly as if poor, even though they possess great riches. Outward appearances rarely reveal a person's true condition. True abundance is found in the soul rather than in worldly show.

A rich man can use his money to buy his way out of danger, but his wealth also makes him a target for extortion. A poor man may have little, but nobody targets him with threats for money. Having fewer earthly possessions often spares a person from many perils.

The life of a righteous person shines like a steady, joyful light that keeps on burning. The wicked have only a tiny, flickering lamp of their own making that will soon be snuffed out. God's truth gives lasting joy that outlives dark times.

Pride is the main root of quarrels and fighting between people. Those who are humble enough to ask for advice and listen to others find wisdom and peace. Letting go of stubbornness quickly puts out the fire of an argument.

Wealth gained through dishonest schemes or gambling soon dwindles away. In contrast, money earned little by little through honest labor steadily grows. God blesses patient work rather than get-rich-quick shortcuts.

Waiting a long time for a delayed dream makes the heart feel sick and weary. When that longing is finally granted, it feels like a tree of life that restores fresh energy and joy. God knows how deeply we feel the ache of waiting.

Anyone who looks down on God's word and ignores His commands heads straight toward ruin. Those who respect God's instructions with loving reverence find safety and lasting reward. Honouring Scripture keeps our lives firmly anchored.

The guidance of wise teachers flows like a fresh spring of water that brings life and renewal. It steers people away from the deadly traps that catch the unwary. Listening to godly counsel helps protect us from moral disaster.

Good judgment and kind conduct win the favor of both God and fellow human beings. But the path of the treacherous is rough and painful, like a rocky, overgrown road. Living in sin always proves to be a hard and exhausting way to live.

Sensible people think ahead and act with knowledge and careful thought. A foolish person rushes ahead and puts his ignorance on full display for everyone to see. True prudence takes time to understand before taking action.

An unreliable messenger creates disaster for his mission and brings trouble on himself. A trustworthy envoy, however, brings relief and resolves difficult problems like healing medicine. Being faithful to our duties brings health to every relationship.

A person who refuses guidance and scorns correction will soon face poverty and dishonour. But anyone who takes constructive criticism to heart earns respect and real honour. Being willing to learn from mistakes paves the way to blessing.

Seeing a good goal reached brings deep satisfaction to the human soul. Yet fools miss out on that joy because they hate giving up their evil habits. Leaving sin behind is the necessary price for true, lasting happiness.

Spending time with wise companions rubs off on us, helping us grow wiser day by day. Hanging around with fools leads to spiritual and moral destruction. The friends we choose will inevitably shape who we become.

Disaster and trouble chase after unrepentant sinners like a hunter pursuing its prey. At the same time, God ensures that those who live uprightly are repaid with lasting good. God will always have the final say on every life.

A good person leaves a lasting legacy of faith, wisdom, and honest resources for children and grandchildren. Meanwhile, the ill-gotten wealth of the wicked ends up passing into the hands of the righteous. A life lived for God blesses future generations.

Even small plots of land worked by the poor can yield plenty of food through diligent effort. Yet unfair treatment and lack of justice can sweep away that harvest in a moment. While honest labor produces good fruit, injustice often robs the vulnerable.

Holding back needed correction from a child does not show true love, but actually harms the child like hatred would. A parent who genuinely loves a child is careful to provide timely, guided discipline. Early training prevents harmful habits from taking deep root.

Upright people are blessed with enough to eat and a contented spirit that is easily satisfied. Wicked people, however, are constantly driven by craving and never feel full. True satisfaction comes from a heart at peace with God.
